title: Florida House, District 99
what_it_does: Represents District 99 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Provisional: Florida Politics reported on June 8, 2026 (four days before candidate qualifying closed at noon June 12) that the incumbent had drawn no opponent. Whether anyone qualified in the final days could NOT be verified in this sandbox (Division of Elections, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia were blocked), so treat 'not on ballot' as provisional.
verified_ballot_note: Florida Politics (June 8, 2026) reported incumbent Democratic Rep. Daryl Campbell had no opposition in HD 99 ahead of the June 12 qualifying deadline (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/800374-with-qualifying-days-away-5-competitive-house-seats-remain-unchallenged/). Final qualifying status not verified. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Daryl Campbell
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Incumbent Democratic state representative for HD 99 (part of Broward: Fort Lauderdale, Lauderhill, Plantation, Wilton Manors). Reported unopposed as of June 8, 2026.

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Voted against CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

sources.title: CS/HJR 1-F (2026) bill page - The Florida Senate

insurance.summary: Voted against SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.

sources.title: SB 2-A (Dec. 2022) bill page - The Florida Senate

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

sources.title: CS/SB 102 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

immigration.summary: Voted against SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.

sources.title: SB 2-C (2025) bill page - The Florida Senate

abortion.summary: Voted against SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: SB 300 (2023) bill page - The Florida Senate

guns.summary: Voted against HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.

record.item: Voted against CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

Voted against SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
Voted against SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted against HB 543 (2023), the 2023 law allowing adults to carry a concealed firearm without a permit.
Voted against HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted against SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.

Voted against SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.
Voted against HB 5 (2022), the 2022 law limiting most abortions to 15 weeks.
Voted against HB 1557 (2022), the 2022 Parental Rights in Education law restricting classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity.

Voted against CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.

Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.
